tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The test starts with a generator-backed POST, producing Transfer-Encoding, and simulates a 302 redirect (tests/test_requests.py:327-341). Requests converts applicable redirect methods to GET (src/requests/sessions.py:333-353), and for statuses other than 307/308 clears the body and its Content-Length, Content-Type, and Transfer-Encoding headers (src/requests/sessions.py:221-232). This is consistency of the rewritten request, not a blanket prohibition on GET bodies or proof of a specific security exploit.

checked_claims.claim: SSL context refactoring addresses builder design
checked_claims.reason: Current configuration accurate, but response only suggests methods and omits requested builder boundary and CERT_OPTIONAL semantics.

material_errors: Current configuration accurate, but response only suggests methods and omits requested builder boundary and CERT_OPTIONAL semantics.
tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: TLSServer currently creates a server SSLContext, loads its certificate/key, and conditionally sets CERT_OPTIONAL and CA trust before wrapping the socket (tests/testserver/server.py:159-176). A proposed SSLContextBuilder can accept those configuration values, create the context, separately load server credentials and client trust/verification settings, then return the configured context. TLSServer would retain socket lifecycle ownership and consume that result. This creates an independently testable configuration boundary but adds an abstraction worth using only if reuse or policy complexity justifies it. Preserve CERT_OPTIONAL in a behavior-preserving refactor; requiring a client certificate is a separate policy change.

checked_claims.reason: Auth needs prepared body and may add hooks; reference falsely says earlier user hooks are necessarily lost despite register_hook appending.

tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: prepare builds method, URL, headers, cookies, and body before auth so authenticators such as OAuth see a prepared request; auth can modify it and content length is recomputed (src/requests/models.py:366-377,597-608). User hooks are prepared after auth, explicitly because authenticators may add hooks. register_hook appends or extends the event list (src/requests/models.py:207-216), so this order places authenticator hooks before subsequently registered user hooks; merely reversing it does not inherently erase hooks. These stateful dependent steps are unsuitable for arbitrary parallelization.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: prepare_body takes a streaming data object as the whole body and explicitly rejects simultaneous files (src/requests/models.py:517-555). The alternative file path uses _encode_files, which reads file objects and assembles multipart data (src/requests/models.py:185-203). Requests does not implement an encoder combining those paths here. Supporting it would require defining how streamed input maps to multipart parts and a suitable encoder, potentially streaming; the limitation is this implementation, not a fundamental prohibition on streaming multipart.

tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: prepare_request converts request cookies to a CookieJar, then merges session cookies and request cookies into a fresh jar (src/requests/sessions.py:467-476). CookieJar merging uses update or set_cookie; the separate dictionary branch uses overwrite=False (src/requests/cookies.py:542-561). Removing the merge without equivalent replacement can omit cookies required jointly by the server and thereby break cookie-based authentication; exact effects depend on which source remains. Redirects also merge session cookies before regenerating the Cookie header (src/requests/sessions.py:234-242). Cookie matching rules still determine which cookies are transmitted.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: CaseInsensitiveDict lowercases the supplied key on set/get/delete and stores the lowercase key alongside the original casing and value (src/requests/structures.py:46-55). That adds work proportional to key processing on each operation, but the source does not establish significant performance degradation. Profile the workload first. For repeated access in an internal hot path, a carefully designed normalized-key lookup interface could reuse a normalized key; a bounded normalization cache is another tradeoff, adding lookup and memory costs. Preserve case-insensitive public semantics and original-key iteration behavior.

material_errors: Warning conversion exists but warnings can be configured as errors; urllib3 code checks major/minor, not asserted 1.21.1 patch bound.
tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: Validation belongs in check_compatibility rather than exception classes. It parses versions and checks urllib3 major >=1 and, for major 1, minor >=21; despite its comment it does not check the 1.21 patch value. It checks chardet in [3.0.2,6.0.0) or charset_normalizer in [2.0.0,4.0.0) (src/requests/__init__.py:58-90). Import-time code converts AssertionError and ValueError into RequestsDependencyWarning (src/requests/__init__.py:107-119), a RequestsWarning subclass (src/requests/exceptions.py:142-151). This normally permits execution while reporting incompatibility; warning filters can turn warnings into errors, and asserts are disabled under optimized Python.
